feed.subtitle: PostDoc Researcher in Urban AI Institute at KAIST & Partner Architect at AR-GE Architects

entry.title: Joining Ar-ge Architects as Partner
entry.content:
I’m excited to announce that I’ve joined Ar-ge Architects as a Partner Architect. This new role represents a fascinating opportunity to bridge my research background in urban analytics with hands-on architectural practice.

The position allows me to continue my research at KAIST while leading design projects that integrate computational methods with traditional architectural practice. I’m particularly interested in how data-driven insights can inform better design decisions and create more responsive built environments.

This dual role as researcher and practitioner feels like a natural evolution of my work on evidence-based urban design. Looking forward to sharing more about projects that emerge from this unique combination of academic rigor and design creativity.
entry.summary: Exciting new chapter combining research expertise with architectural practice.

entry.title: G-School Best Innovation Award at KAIST-NYU Young Researcher Day

link.title: G-School Best Innovation Award at KAIST-NYU Young Researcher Day

entry.content:
Honored to receive the G-School Best Innovation Award for “Spatial Awareness in Deep Learning: Approaches to Integrating Geolocational Attributes in Deep Learning Models” at the KAIST-NYU Young Researcher Day.

This research explores how to better integrate spatial and geographical context into deep learning models for urban analytics. Traditional machine learning often treats spatial data as just another feature, but geographic relationships have unique properties that deserve special consideration.

The work has implications for urban prediction models, mobility analysis, and smart city applications. It’s encouraging to see recognition for research that sits at the intersection of computer science and urban studies.

The collaboration with NYU’s Urban X program has been invaluable for developing these ideas. Looking forward to pushing this research further and exploring practical applications in urban planning and design.
entry.summary: Recognition for spatial awareness in deep learning research at Urban X collaboration.

entry.title: Developing AI Models for Local Airbnb Market Prediction

link.title: Developing AI Models for Local Airbnb Market Prediction

entry.content:
Working on an interesting challenge: can we predict monthly changes in local Airbnb markets using only publicly available data? This research, which I’ll be presenting at the International Conference on Tourism Research in 2025, attempts to answer that question.

The motivation comes from urban planning needs. Cities worldwide are grappling with the impacts of short-term rentals on housing markets and neighborhoods. Better prediction tools could help policymakers understand and respond to these changes more effectively.

Our approach integrates multiple public data sources - transportation networks, demographic indicators, seasonal patterns, and urban infrastructure data - to create monthly predictions at the neighborhood level. Early results are promising, with accuracy rates above 85%.

What’s particularly interesting is how transportation accessibility emerges as a key predictor. Areas with good public transit connections show different Airbnb market dynamics than more isolated neighborhoods. This suggests urban infrastructure decisions have lasting effects on tourism patterns.

The research also highlights the value of open data initiatives. Much of this analysis wouldn’t be possible without cities making datasets publicly available.
entry.summary: New research on predicting short-term rental market dynamics using public datasets.
